beats.narration: Begin by framing Lesson Title: CSCI-620: Introduction to Big Data as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. This course provides a broad introduction to the exploration and management of large datasets being generated and used in the modern world. Consider this worked case: Case studies examine urban crime, drug research, census data, social networking, and space exploration. On screen, display a slide with the course title and a grid of icons representing the five case study domains (crime, drug research, census, social networking, space exploration). List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.

beats.narration: Now define Lesson Title: Lesson 1: Foundations of Big Data precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Prereq: (CSCI-603 or CSCI-605 with a grade of B or better) or (CSCI-320 or SWEN-344). Consider this worked case: Students must verify their prerequisite status before enrolling in the course. On screen, show a checklist graphic with the prerequisite courses listed and a checkbox for each. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a checklist graphic with the prerequisite courses listed and a checkbox for each.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Lesson Title: Lesson 2: Internet Protocol Suite Overview operates in a concrete sequence. Internet hosts implement layered link, internet, transport, and application functions. Consider this worked case: The link layer moves frames across a directly connected network, while IP provides best-effort datagram delivery across interconnected networks. On screen, draw a four-layer stack diagram with labels for link, internet, transport, and application layers, pointing to each layer's function. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Draw a four-layer stack diagram with labels for link, internet, transport, and application layers, pointing to each layer's function.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Lesson Title: Lesson 3: IP Addressing and Routing and make the decision criteria explicit. Routing selects a next hop toward a destination. Consider this worked case: When a packet is sent, the router examines the IP address to determine the optimal path to the destination interface. On screen, illustrate a network diagram with two routers, highlighting the IP address on an interface and an arrow showing the next hop selection process. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
beats.title: Lesson Title: Lesson 3: IP Addressing and Routing
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a network diagram with two routers, highlighting the IP address on an interface and an arrow showing the next hop selection process.

beats.narration: Apply Lesson Title: Lesson 4: Transport Protocol Functions to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. Transport protocols add endpoint communication functions above IP. Consider this worked case: Application protocols define the meaning of exchanged data, while transport protocols handle the reliable delivery mechanism. On screen, show a simplified TCP/IP model with the transport layer positioned above IP, labeled with 'endpoint communication functions' and 'application protocols' above it. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a simplified TCP/IP model with the transport layer positioned above IP, labeled with 'endpoint communication functions' and 'application protocols' above it.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Lesson Title: Lesson 5: TCP Reliability and Byte Streams, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. TCP provides a reliable, ordered byte stream between endpoints. Consider this worked case: Sequence numbers identify positions in that byte stream, allowing the receiver to reconstruct the original data order. On screen, display a sequence of numbered packets (1, 2, 3) arriving at a receiver, with a visual indicator showing how sequence numbers restore order. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a sequence of numbered packets (1, 2, 3) arriving at a receiver, with a visual indicator showing how sequence numbers restore order.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Lesson Title: Lesson 6: TCP Acknowledgments and Retransmission with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Acknowledgments report which data has been received. Consider this worked case: If a packet is lost, the receiver sends an acknowledgment indicating the gap, prompting the sender to retransmit the missing data. On screen, create a timeline graphic showing packet transmission, a missing packet, an acknowledgment signal, and a retransmission arrow. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.

beats.narration: Use Lesson Title: Lesson 7: TCP Flow Control and State Management to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Flow control prevents a sender from exceeding the receiver's advertised capacity. Consider this worked case: Before application data transfer, connection establishment synchronizes endpoint state to ensure both sides are ready. On screen, show a state machine diagram with states like 'Establishment', 'Data Transfer', and 'Termination', with arrows indicating transitions. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.

beats.narration: Connect Lesson Title: Lesson 8: Data Preparation and Visualization to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. First, practical techniques used in exploratory data analysis and mining are introduced; topics include data preparation, visualization, statistics for understanding data, and grouping and prediction techniques. Consider this worked case: Cleaning and organizing raw datasets allows analysts to identify patterns and trends through visual representations. On screen, present a before-and-after comparison of a messy dataset and a cleaned, visualized chart (e.g., bar graph or scatter plot). Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.

beats.narration: Finish with Lesson Title: Lesson 9: Statistics and Grouping/Prediction Techniques as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Retransmission recovers data that is presumed lost. Consider this worked case: Statistical methods help quantify uncertainty, while grouping and prediction techniques identify clusters and forecast future values. On screen, display a split screen showing a statistical summary table on the left and a clustering/prediction model output on the right. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.

sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.excerpt: This course provides a broad introduction to the exploration and management of large datasets being generated and used in the modern world. First, practical techniques used in exploratory data analysis and mining are introduced; topics include data preparation, visualization, statistics for understanding data, and grouping and prediction techniques. Second, approaches used to store, retrieve, and manage data in the real world are presented; topics include traditional database systems, query languages, and data integrity and quality. Case studies will examine issues in data capture, organization, storage, retrieval, visualization, and analysis in diverse settings such as urban crime, drug research, census data, social networking, and space exploration. sources.author: Internet Engineering Task Force
sources.excerpt: Internet hosts implement layered link, internet, transport, and application functions. The link layer moves frames across a directly connected network. IP provides best-effort datagram delivery across interconnected networks. An IP address identifies an interface for internet-layer delivery. Routing selects a next hop toward a destination. Transport protocols add endpoint communication functions above IP. Application protocols define the meaning of exchanged data. Correct analysis distinguishes addresses, routes, packets, frames, sockets, and end-to-end state.
sources.title: RFC 1122 Requirements for Internet Hosts

sources.author: Internet Engineering Task Force
sources.excerpt: TCP provides a reliable, ordered byte stream between endpoints. Sequence numbers identify positions in that byte stream. Acknowledgments report which data has been received. Retransmission recovers data that is presumed lost. Flow control prevents a sender from exceeding the receiver's advertised capacity. A TCP connection moves through defined protocol states. Connection establishment synchronizes endpoint state before application data transfer. Packet loss, duplication, reordering, delay, and endpoint failure must be separated when reasoning about behavior and performance.
